newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil's Statfjord A in brief shutdown.
newsitem.headline: Statoil's Statfjord A in brief shutdown.

text.p: Crude production at the North Sea Statfjord A platform was halted for two hours last Thursday due to a fault in a heat alarm, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Tuesday.
The unscheduled shutdown also closed output at the nearby Snorre field, Statoil said.
"Production at Statfjord A was close on July 3 at 8.04 a.m. (0604 GMT) because of a fault in a heat alarm. This also closed the Snorre field," a Statoil spokesman said.
"Statfjord A was back up at 10 am (0800 GMT) and Snorre resumed production at 13.07 (1107 GMT)."
Statfjord A has an average throughput of around 110,000 barrels per day (bpd), while Saga Petroleum's Snorre pumps about 200,000 bpd.
